# Dialogue cleanup: hum, hiss and clicks out

A noisy dialogue take played twice: first raw, with mains hum, hiss and clicks, then after the cleanup chain (declick, rumble-reduction EQ, noise gate, compressor). The two waveforms show the noise floor between phrases disappear while the voice stays.

- Type: Dialogue cleanup
- Skill: `magnifito-audio`
- Engine: `declick, eq, noise-gate, compress-audio`
- Output: 1920x1080, 12 s, with audio
- Video: [`../videos/f22-dialogue-cleanup.mp4`](../videos/f22-dialogue-cleanup.mp4)

## Recreate it with Claude Code

Install the plugin (see the repository README), open this folder, and give Claude this prompt:

> Generate 6 seconds of synthetic noisy dialogue (make-audio.mjs: a voice-like tone track, no real speech, with 50 Hz mains hum and its harmonics, hiss and random clicks). Clean it up with the audio skill: remove the clicks first, then cut the hum with the rumble-reduction EQ, gate the hiss in the pauses (threshold -26 dB, ratio 8; after the EQ so the hum cannot hold the gate open) and level it with the broadcast-master compressor. Make a 12-second before/after clip on the Magnifito cream background (panels.svg, Geist from fonts/): the raw take plays first under its waveform, then the clean take under its waveform, with a playhead and the active panel highlighted.

## Recreate it by hand

From the repository root, one command renders this example exactly as committed:

```sh
npm run showcase -- f22-dialogue-cleanup
```

Or run the steps yourself from `showcase/f22-dialogue-cleanup/` (after `npm run build && npm link`):

```sh
node make-audio.mjs
mgvideo declick work/noisy.wav --out work/declicked.wav
mgvideo eq work/declicked.wav --preset rumble-reduction --out work/eq.wav
mgvideo noise-gate work/eq.wav --threshold -26 --ratio 8 --out work/gated.wav
mgvideo compress-audio work/gated.wav --preset broadcast-master --out work/clean.wav
mgvideo waveform work/noisy.wav --width 1600 --height 280 --color '#7a584c' --out work/wave-before.png
mgvideo waveform work/clean.wav --width 1600 --height 280 --color '#7a584c' --out work/wave-after.png
node rasterize.mjs panels.svg work/panels.png 1920 1080
ffmpeg -loop 1 -framerate 30 -t 12 -i work/panels.png -i work/wave-before.png -i work/wave-after.png -i work/noisy.wav -i work/clean.wav -filter_complex "[0:v][1:v]overlay=160:210[v1];[v1][2:v]overlay=160:660,drawbox=x=140:y=640:w=1640:h=320:color=0xf0eadf@0.6:t=fill:enable='lt(t,6)',drawbox=x=140:y=190:w=1640:h=320:color=0xf0eadf@0.6:t=fill:enable='gte(t,6)',drawbox=x=140:y=190:w=10:h=320:color=0x8acf31:t=fill:enable='lt(t,6)',drawbox=x=140:y=640:w=10:h=320:color=0x8acf31:t=fill:enable='gte(t,6)'[bg];color=c=0x2b1c17:s=4x300:r=30:d=12,split[p1][p2];[bg][p1]overlay=x='160+1600*t/6':y=200:enable='lt(t,6)'[bg2];[bg2][p2]overlay=x='160+1600*(t-6)/6':y=650:enable='gte(t,6)',format=yuv420p[v];[3:a][4:a]concat=n=2:v=0:a=1,aformat=sample_rates=48000:channel_layouts=stereo[a]" -map [v] -map [a] -t 12 -c:v libx264 -crf 16 -preset medium -c:a aac -b:a 160k work/compare.mp4
```

The finished file is `work/compare.mp4`. The config files in this folder are the inputs.
